data.title: 6 US Stocks to Watch After Wall Street's $2.5 Trillion Crash
data.description: Nasdaq market value fell roughly $2.5 trillion Thursday as investors sold AI stocks; a modest Friday rebound failed to prevent a fourth straight weekly decline. According to BeInCrypto, NVIDIA, Vistra, Amazon, Alphabet, Uber and Netflix are stocks to watch based on earnings, valuations and Wall Street forecasts. NVIDIA fell 9.3% Thursday despite revenue doubling to $96.2 billion; Vistra gained 10.5% Friday as adjusted EBITDA rose 50%. Amazon cloud revenue grew 39.3%, Alphabet revenue rose 25% and cloud sales more than doubled, Uber bookings climbed 20% with $2.5 billion in free cash flow, and Netflix revenue grew 12%. All six have bullish consensus ratings, though infrastructure restrictions, heavy spending, weaker guidance and slower ad growth pose risks.

data.title: FIGS CEO Trina Spear Says Demand Outstrips Supply as Results Beat Estimates
data.description:
FIGS reported third-quarter revenue of $190.7 million, above the $182.8 million estimate, and top- and bottom-line results exceeded expectations, according to Bloomberg. The company recorded a fourth consecutive quarter of at least 25% revenue growth. Non-scrubwear revenue rose 35%, and international revenue also increased.

CEO and co-founder Trina Spear said health care professionals are buying more FIGS products beyond scrubs, including underscrubs, compression socks and outerwear, for work and off-duty wear.

data.title: AI | Groq Executive Targets Doubling Valuation to $8 Billion Amid AI Selloff
data.description: A Groq executive has launched a bid to double the data center operator’s valuation to $8 billion in about three months, according to Bloomberg. The executive criticized rivals for relying too heavily on debt markets.

data.title: Hyperliquid Burns $1.64 Million Worth of HYPE in 24 Hours, Repurchasing 21,040 Tokens
data.description: Hyperliquid repurchased and burned 21,040 HYPE in 24 hours, worth $1.64 million, at an average price of $77.93. According to Odaily, Onchain Lens reported the figures.

data.title: Arini Flagship Fund’s Year-to-Date Loss Widens to 32% as It Sells Holdings
data.description:
Arini Capital Management’s flagship hedge fund’s year-to-date loss widened to 32% by the final days of October, and it sold some holdings.

According to Sina Finance, citing a letter to investors, the fund, which focuses on high-yield debt, lost 19.7% in October amid continued weakness in credit markets. Managed by Hamza Lemssouguer, the fund reassessed its five largest positions, which together represented about two-thirds of its net asset value.

The fund received $389 million in inflows over the past week, part of its $1.5 billion fundraising. The letter said the fund had underestimated dislocations in the CCC-rated bond market, which accounted for most of its exposure and led to strong co-movement among portfolio positions. The fund cut some positions and reduced total leverage to its lowest level since early 2022, while planning to further diversify its portfolio.

data.title: AI | AI-Animated Feature 'Gods Don’t Give Gifts' Set for Theaters
data.description: The AI-generated animated feature Gods Don’t Give Gifts is heading to theaters. Fable Studio CEO Edward Saatchi said a team of 30 people spent nine months creating the film, which relies on human directors, writers, voice actors and artists, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Paraguay Senate Removes President Santiago Peña Over Banking Scandal
data.description: Paraguay's Senate voted unanimously to remove President Santiago Peña over a banking scandal on Friday, Senate TV reported. According to Sina Finance, citing Senate TV, the impeachment motion passed with 44 votes in favor and one abstention.

data.title: Tom Lee Sees 15% Nasdaq Rally as JPMorgan's Jack Caffrey Calls AI Rout Normal
data.description: Fundstrat’s Tom Lee said he would buy the AI-stock dip and expects a 15% Nasdaq rally, while JPMorgan Asset Management portfolio manager Jack Caffrey called the selloff normal. The Nasdaq-100 fell 6.36% and erased $2.3 trillion in value a day earlier, according to BeInCrypto. Caffrey said companies he met this week had 12- to 24-month order backlogs. On Friday, US payrolls rose 165,000 in October, versus roughly 65,000 expected, lifting bets on a December Fed rate hike.

data.description: Circle minted 250 million USDC on Solana, and Solscan data shows the transaction was executed by Circle’s minting address. According to Odaily, Whale Alert recorded the mint at 6:06 (UTC+8).

data.title: Ukraine Clarifies Budanov Will Attend Ukraine-U.S.-Russia Talks but Will Not Lead Delegation
data.description: Ukraine President's Office Chief Budanov will attend trilateral talks with the United States and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, but will not lead Ukraine's delegation. According to Sina Finance, citing China Media Group, presidential press adviser Litvin said on November 6 that Budanov had only confirmed he would travel to Abu Dhabi with the Ukrainian delegation, not that he would lead it; Ukraine's negotiating team was preparing for the talks, and the parties had held several rounds of discussions on arrangements that day.

data.title: Zelenskyy Says Ukraine Will Continue Strikes on Russian Oil Refineries
data.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on social media on the evening of the 6th that Ukraine would continue striking Russian oil refineries in response to Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. According to Sina Finance, Zelenskyy said he had received reports that day from Ukraine’s defense and security forces about long-range strikes, and that Russian drones and missiles continued to target Ukrainian power plants, the electricity grid, heating systems, water facilities, and civilian logistics.

Zelenskyy said Russia had rejected de-escalation measures proposed by Ukraine’s partners and planned further attacks, adding that Ukraine had determined its response. He said Ukrainian long- and medium-range strikes, along with full pressure from its partners, would create momentum for “genuine negotiations.”

Russian presidential press secretary Peskov told media on the 3rd that Ukrainian forces continued to attack Russian energy infrastructure, while Russia continued “systematic strikes” on Ukrainian infrastructure to weaken Ukraine’s ability to attack Russia. Peskov also confirmed that trilateral talks involving Russia, the United States, and Ukraine on the Ukraine issue would be held in Abu Dhabi on the 10th and 11th.

data.title: Ukraine Sets Priorities for Abu Dhabi Talks; Budanov Does Not Expect a Breakthrough
data.description:
Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on November 6 that Kyiv's priorities for the upcoming trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi are security guarantees, de-escalation in the Black Sea, an energy ceasefire, the return of Ukrainian children and prisoner exchanges.

According to Sina Finance, citing China Media Group, Sybiha said Ukraine hopes Russia will show equal commitment to the peace process and called for Europe's full participation. He said arrangements concerning Ukraine must not bypass Kyiv, decisions on European security should not be made without Europe, and Europe should take part in all coordination before and after the Abu Dhabi talks.

Sybiha said Russia continues to intensify strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities and pressure on the front, causing many Ukrainian civilian casualties. He said Ukraine would continue long-range strikes on Russian territory.

Budanov, head of Ukraine's presidential office, said he did not expect a breakthrough from the Abu Dhabi talks, but viewed the two sides' agreement to resume face-to-face talks after several months as progress. He said the talks were neither final nor decisive and would address preparations for ending the current war; he declined to assess their possible outcome.

U.S. presidential envoy Steve Witkoff said on social media on the 2nd that the United States would mediate working-level talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on the 10th and 11th. The agenda would include postwar security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian action and further steps toward peace. The talks would mark the resumption of trilateral discussions on the conflict among Russia, the United States and Ukraine after nine months.

data.title: Putin Confirms Russia-U.S.-Ukraine Talks Will Be Held in Abu Dhabi on November 10
data.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin confirmed on November 6 that trilateral talks on Ukraine involving Russia, the United States and Ukraine will be held in Abu Dhabi, the UAE capital, on November 10. According to Sina Finance, Putin said members of the Russian delegation attended a meeting of Russia’s Security Council that day. Participants included presidential aides Medinsky and Ushakov, Kostyukov, head of the Main Intelligence Directorate of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces, and Deputy Foreign Ministers Galuzin and Ryabkov. The meeting discussed arrangements for the upcoming trilateral talks, and Putin thanked the UAE leadership for its efforts to help resolve the Ukraine crisis.

data.title: STOCKS | Dow Falls 0.46% to 51,285.73; S&P 500 Rises 0.31% to 7,376.85 on November 6
data.description: According to Jin10, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 237.33 points, or 0.46%, to 51,285.73 on Friday, November 6, while the S&P 500 rose 23.12 points, or 0.31%, to 7,376.85, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 264.43 points, or 1.09%, to 24,579.42.

data.title: Kazuo Ueda: Bank of Japan May Resume QE Tools After a Severe Shock
data.description: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda, one of the pioneers of quantitative easing in the late 1990s, said the central bank might use unconventional policy tools again if Japan faces a major shock. According to Sina Finance, Ueda said the measures had produced some positive effects on the economy and inflation but were not a perfect substitute for interest-rate cuts when rates are positive. He added that the Bank of Japan might have to use the tools again depending on the severity of a shock, and should consider how to minimize negative side effects, including effects on market functioning.

data.title: Fidelity Transfers 27,000 ETH to Galaxy Digital With Plans to Sell
data.description: Fidelity transferred 27,000 ETH to Galaxy Digital and plans to sell it. According to Odaily, Onchain Lens reported that Fidelity had just transferred an additional 10,000 ETH for a potential sale, bringing its total transfers today to 27,000 ETH.

data.title: International Oil Prices Edge Higher on the 6th
data.description: According to Jin10, at the close on the 6th, December light crude futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange rose 31 cents to $90.83 per barrel, up 0.34%, while January Brent crude futures in London gained 3 cents to $98.32 per barrel, up 0.03%.

data.title: Supreme Court to Weigh Goldman Sachs Bid on Bankruptcy Arbitration
data.description: The U.S. Supreme Court agreed to review Goldman Sachs' request to determine whether bankruptcy courts can override arbitration agreements, setting up a test of the Federal Arbitration Act's reach, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI | AI-Linked Trade Recovers After Historic Tech Stock Rout
data.description: The AI trade rebounded after a historic rout in technology stocks, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Braskem Shareholders Withdraw Proposed Funding as Debt Talks Sour
data.description: Braskem SA's shareholders have taken a proposed capital injection off the table as the company's talks with creditors over an out-of-court debt restructuring soured, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
